title: The documented pod fails on an SELinux host, exiting 139 with no log line
foundBy: session agent, following README.md and INSTALL.md as a first-time reader

evidence.verified: Played the stock spec from a world-traversable directory: pod Degraded, container exit 139, no logs. After `chcon -t container_file_t -l s0 bin/cs-vcr` the same spec runs, and a POST of cassettes/claude-code-subscription/req/0001.json through the published port returned HTTP 200.

details:
INSTALL.md's container section is two commands: `make build-go` then `podman kube play deploy/vcr.yaml`. On Fedora with SELinux enforcing the pod reports `Degraded`, the container exits 139, and `podman logs` is empty, so nothing says why.

`podman kube play` gives a hostPath **directory** a shared SELinux label and leaves a hostPath naming a **file** alone. Measured on this host before and after playing the spec:

```
bin/cs-vcr   user_tmp_t        (unchanged)
cassettes    container_file_t  (relabelled)
```

So the container cannot execute the binary it was mounted. Relabelling the binary alone fixes it, and the pod then serves a recorded step. A plain `chcon -t container_file_t` is not always enough: it keeps whatever MCS category a previous container left on the file, and `-l s0` clears it.

The pod spec's header already warns that the store has to be readable by uid 65532, which is the same class of host detail.
